WhyOrdo.title: Why Ordo Todo?
WhyOrdo.subtitle: We built Ordo Todo to be the productivity tool we always wanted. Here's what makes us different.

all_in_one.title: All-in-One Platform
all_in_one.description: Tasks, projects, time tracking, and analytics in one place. No more switching between apps.

cross_platform.title: True Cross-Platform
cross_platform.description: Web, Desktop (Windows, Mac, Linux), and Mobile (iOS, Android). Your data syncs everywhere.

privacy.title: Privacy-First
privacy.description: Your data stays yours. Sign in with your account (Google/GitHub OAuth or password), encryption in transit (TLS), and workspace-scoped access controls. No data selling. Ever.

ai_helps.title: AI That Helps, Not Takes Over
ai_helps.description: Smart suggestions and automation when you want it. You're always in control.

no_lockin.title: No Subscription Lock-in
no_lockin.description: Generous free tier. Export your data anytime. Fair, transparent pricing.

focus_builtin.title: Focus Mode Built-in
focus_builtin.description: Pomodoro timer and deep work tools integrated directly. No extra apps needed.

StarFeatures.title: Features That Make a Difference
StarFeatures.subtitle: Powerful tools designed for real productivity. These are the features our users love most.

eisenhower.title: Eisenhower Matrix
eisenhower.description: Prioritize tasks by urgency and importance. See at a glance what needs your attention now.

kanban.title: Kanban Boards
kanban.description: Visualize your workflow with flexible boards. Drag and drop tasks between columns.

time_blocking.title: Time Blocking
time_blocking.description: Schedule tasks in your calendar. Block time for deep work and protect your productivity.

focus_timer.title: Focus Timer
focus_timer.description: Built-in Pomodoro timer with customizable sessions. Track your focus time and take smart breaks.

okrs.title: OKRs & Goals
okrs.description: Set objectives and key results. Track progress on what matters most to you.

collaboration.title: Team Collaboration
collaboration.description: Invite team members, assign tasks, and work together seamlessly in shared workspaces.

AIFeatures.title: Supercharged by
AIFeatures.subtitle: Our AI works behind the scenes to help you be more productive. Smart features that learn from your habits.

smart_scheduling.title: Smart Scheduling
smart_scheduling.description: AI analyzes your patterns and suggests the best times for each task. Work when you're most effective.

priority_intelligence.title: Priority Intelligence
priority_intelligence.description: Automatically prioritizes tasks based on deadlines, importance, and your work patterns.

burnout_prevention.title: Burnout Prevention
burnout_prevention.description: Detects when you're overloaded and suggests rest. Protects your long-term productivity.

weekly_reports.title: Weekly Reports
weekly_reports.description: AI-generated insights about your productivity. See trends and get personalized tips.

energy_matching.title: Energy Matching
energy_matching.description: Matches tasks to your energy levels. High-focus work when you're sharp, routine when you're not.

task_estimation.title: Task Estimation
task_estimation.description: AI predicts how long tasks will take based on similar tasks you've completed before.

AIFeatures.ai_statement: AI analyzes your tasks through an external provider (Google Gemini). You can turn AI features on or off in settings.

FAQ.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about Ordo Todo.

fallback.billing_trial_a: Yes: 14 days of Pro with no card required. When it ends, add a card to stay on Pro or keep using Free.
fallback.billing_grace_q: What happens if a payment fails?
fallback.billing_grace_a: Everything keeps working for 14 days while we retry the payment. Then the account moves to Free. Reading and exporting your data are never blocked.
fallback.billing_live_a: Not yet: all features are currently free while paid plans are in beta. We will announce payment methods before charging anything.
fallback.agents_what_q: Can my AI assistant use Ordo?
fallback.agents_what_a: Yes: ChatGPT, Claude, Hermes and OpenClaw connect in under 60 seconds with 17 tools. See the connection guides.
fallback.agents_permissions_a: Only what you can see: every request runs with your permissions and unauthorized access is denied.
fallback.agents_own_q: Does Ordo have its own agent?
fallback.agents_own_a: Yes: ask questions about your workspace with cited answers, run actions in plain language, and schedule recurrent jobs.

Guide.title: Getting Started

header.title: User Guide
header.subtitle: Everything you need to master Ordo Todo

sidebar.community_text: Join our community for tips and support.

main.welcome_text: This guide will help you get up and running in just a few minutes. Our app combines powerful task management with focus tools to help you achieve your goals.

1.title: Create your account
1.description: Sign up for free and set up your profile. Choose your timezone and preferred language.

2.title: Create a Workspace
2.description: Workspaces help you separate different areas of your life. Create one for Personal and one for Work.

3.title: Add your first Project
3.description: Projects organize related tasks. Create a project for each major goal or initiative.

4.title: Create Tasks
4.description: Break down your projects into actionable tasks. Add due dates, priorities, and estimated time.

5.title: Start the Focus Timer
5.description: Select a task and start the Pomodoro timer. Stay focused for 25 minutes, then take a 5-minute break.

main.pro_tip_end: to quickly create new tasks from anywhere in the app!
main.explore_text: Dive deeper into specific features with these detailed guides, ordered from first steps to power use:

level1.title: Level 1 — First steps
level1.description: Set up and capture your first tasks.

projects.title: Projects & Boards
projects.description: Learn how to organize work with Kanban boards

connect.title: Connect your assistant
connect.description: Use Ordo from ChatGPT, Claude, Hermes or OpenClaw

more_features.title: Discover more
more_features.description: AI meetings, workload, wellbeing, search, coach, gamification and audio.

capture.title: Quick Capture
capture.description: Natural language, Quick-Add and command palette

calendar.title: Calendar Sync
calendar.description: Two-way sync with Google and Outlook

agent.title: Your Own Agent
agent.description: Ask, act and schedule in plain language

scheduling.title: Auto-Scheduling
scheduling.description: Do Date, day plan and risk alerts

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: Create teams, invite people and control roles

notes.title: Sticky Notes
notes.description: Wall and board for your loose ideas

goals.title: Goals (OKRs)
goals.description: Big goals measured with key results

meetings.title: AI Meetings
meetings.description: From transcript to tasks in one click

coach.title: Coach Chat
coach.description: Ask for advice to plan and decide

GuideAgent.title: Your Own Agent
GuideAgent.subtitle: Ask about your workspace, run actions in plain language, and schedule recurrent jobs.

ask.title: Ask anything
ask.description: Questions answered from your tasks, projects and notes — with citations to the source.

actions.title: Act in plain language
actions.description: Propose a plan, review it, then execute: create, update and complete without clicking.
actions.example: Move all design tasks to Friday

jobs.title: Recurrent jobs
jobs.description: Schedule briefings and summaries in natural language; run, pause or delete anytime.

GuideAgent.safety_text: Actions run with your permissions, every step is audited, and destructive plans ask first. Nothing runs silently.
GuideAgent.pro_tip_text: Start with ask: learn what the agent knows before handing it actions.

GuideScheduling.title: Auto-Scheduling
GuideScheduling.subtitle: A proposed day plan with Do Date vs Due Date, automatic replanning and risk alerts.
GuideScheduling.doday_title: Do Date is not Due Date
GuideScheduling.doday_text: Due date is the deadline. Do Date is when you plan to do the work. The planner schedules by Do Date and warns when the deadline is at risk.
GuideScheduling.doday_card_text: Set per task. Tasks without one are scheduled around the ones that have it.
GuideScheduling.replan_card_text: Day start, task completed or overrun: the plan rebuilds itself.

steps.1: Open My plan for today in the morning
steps.2: Review the proposed blocks and freeze the ones you like
steps.3: Apply the plan; tasks get their Do Dates

GuideScheduling.risks_text: Overload and deadline-at-risk warnings arrive with options: move, split, delegate — you decide.
GuideScheduling.pro_tip_text: Durations improve over time: predictions learn from your own completed sessions.

GuideRitual.title: Daily Ritual
GuideRitual.subtitle: Two minutes in the morning, two in the evening: plan the day, then shut it down.
GuideRitual.morning_text: Review today, accept or adjust the proposed timeboxes, and start with intent.
GuideRitual.evening_text: Close the day: completed, carried over, and moves for what's left.

steps.1: Morning ritual proposes your day plan
steps.2: Accept the timeboxes or adjust them
steps.3: Work the plan; the timer and scheduling adapt
steps.4: Evening ritual closes completed and carries the rest

GuideRitual.streak_card_text: Consecutive days with morning or evening done. A skipped or missing day breaks the streak — it restarts honestly.
GuideRitual.reminders_card_text: Gentle nudges if morning or evening is still open.
GuideRitual.pro_tip_text: Pair the ritual with the day plan: accept timeboxes in the morning, review them in the evening.

GuideCapture.title: Quick Capture
GuideCapture.subtitle: Get ideas out of your head in seconds: natural language, Quick-Add and the command palette.
GuideCapture.nl_text: Type a task with date, time, priority and project in one line. Ordo parses dates, recurrence, priorities and project hints automatically.
GuideCapture.nl_result: → Task “Call Ana”, due tomorrow 15:00, high priority, project “work”.

quickadd.title: Quick-Add
quickadd.description: The fastest way: a dialog with live parsing preview.

palette.title: Command palette
palette.description: Navigate and create without touching the mouse.

mobile.title: Mobile
mobile.description: Floating button with the same live parsing.

GuideCapture.palette_text: Eight canonical actions on web and desktop: go to dashboard, tasks, projects or calendar; new task; new project; start timer; search. Type to filter, Enter runs, Esc closes.
GuideCapture.pro_tip_text: Press Tab inside Quick-Add to cycle the inferred fields (date, priority, project) before saving.

GuideCalendar.title: Calendar Sync
GuideCalendar.subtitle: Two-way sync with Google Calendar and Outlook: your tasks on the calendar, your meetings as context.

steps.1: Open Settings → Calendar and choose Google or Microsoft
steps.2: Approve access in the provider window
steps.3: Pick which Ordo projects sync to which calendar

GuideCalendar.push_text: Tasks with dates appear as events on your calendar so your day shows work and meetings together.
GuideCalendar.pull_text: Meetings become busy blocks that the day planner respects when scheduling your tasks.
GuideCalendar.conflicts_text: Last change wins by timestamp, and each connection shows its status (ok, error, re-auth needed). Reconnect from Settings if access expires.
GuideCalendar.pro_tip_text: Give tasks a Do Date (when you will do it), not just a due date, to see them on the calendar.

GuideSlack.title: Slack Integration
GuideSlack.subtitle: Create tasks without leaving Slack: slash command, message actions and daily digest.

command.title: Slash command
command.description: Create tasks and check your day from any channel.

action.title: Message action
action.description: Turn any message into a task with “Create task in Ordo”.

digest.title: Daily digest
digest.description: A briefing with due tasks and recent completions in your channel.

GuideSlack.status_text: When you start a focus session, your Slack status shows you are focusing so the team knows not to disturb. Enable it in Settings (opt-in).
GuideSlack.pro_tip_text: Use /ordo today every morning to see what is due without opening the app.

GuideHabits.title: Habits & Streaks
GuideHabits.subtitle: Small daily actions, compounded. Track habits and keep the streak alive.

steps.1: Open Habits and create a new habit with a name and frequency
steps.2: Complete it each day from the habits view
steps.3: Watch your streak grow in stats

streaks.title: Streaks
streaks.description: Consecutive days completed. A missed day resets the count.

pause.title: Pause
pause.description: Pause a habit for vacations or rest without losing history.

stats.title: Stats
stats.description: Completion rate and history per habit.

GuideHabits.complete_text: Mark each habit done once per day. Completions count toward XP and achievements.
GuideHabits.pro_tip_text: Start with one habit. A 7-day streak earns bonus XP.

GuidePomodoro.title: Pomodoro Deep Dive
GuidePomodoro.subtitle: One timer engine on web, desktop and mobile: modes, task switching and history.
GuidePomodoro.modes_text: Use Pomodoro cycles (25 focus, 5 rest, longer rest every 4) or a continuous timer for open-ended work. Both share the same history and stats.

start.title: Start
start.description: Pick a task and start the timer from any platform.

pause.title: Pause & resume
pause.description: Pause for interruptions and resume the same session.

history.title: History
history.description: Every session is recorded with task, duration and focus score.

GuidePomodoro.task_text: Switch the active task without stopping the timer: the session keeps its data and attributes the new segment to the new task.
GuidePomodoro.platforms_text: Web, desktop (with floating timer) and mobile share one engine, so a session started on one platform keeps its state and history everywhere.
GuidePomodoro.pro_tip_text: Attach the timer to a task to see focus time per task in analytics.

GuideFocus.title: Focus Timer & Pomodoro
GuideFocus.subtitle: Stay in the flow with our built-in Pomodoro timer.
GuideFocus.pomodoro_text: The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method that breaks work into focused intervals (traditionally 25 minutes) separated by short breaks. It's proven to improve focus and prevent burnout.

focus.title: Focus Session
focus.description: Deep work on a single task. No distractions allowed.

short.title: Short Break
short.description: Quick rest to recharge. Stretch, hydrate, relax.

long.title: Long Break
long.description: Extended rest after 4 focus sessions. Go for a walk!

steps.1: Select a task from your list
steps.2: Click "Start Focus" to begin the timer

GuideFocus.pro_tip_text: Enable "Focus Mode" in settings to hide all notifications and distractions during your focus sessions. Your productivity will thank you!
GuideFocus.shortcuts_note: The timer is controlled with on-screen buttons. Global keyboard shortcuts are in the tasks guide.
GuideFocus.audio_note: The app includes locally generated ambient audio to accompany your sessions, with no external subscriptions.

GuideProjects.title: Projects & Kanban Boards
GuideProjects.subtitle: Organize your work visually with flexible boards and lists.
GuideProjects.managing_text: Projects in Ordo Todo allow you to group related tasks together. Whether you're launching a product, planning a vacation, or managing a team, Projects keep everything organized in one place.

creating_steps.1: Click the + New Project button in the sidebar
creating_steps.2: Give your project a descriptive name
creating_steps.3: Choose a color for easy identification
creating_steps.4: Select a workflow template (or start blank)

GuideProjects.views_text: Switch between different views to match your workflow:

kanban.title: Kanban Board
kanban.description: Visualize your workflow with columns. Drag and drop cards to update status instantly.

list.title: List View
list.description: A structured, dense list perfect for reviewing many tasks at once. Great for sorting and filtering.

tags.title: Tags & Labels
tags.description: Categorize tasks with colored tags like "Design", "Marketing", or "Backend".

team.title: Team Collaboration
team.description: Invite team members and assign tasks. Everyone stays in sync.

GuideProjects.pro_tip_end: Use the view buttons above the project to quickly switch between Kanban and List.

GuideTasks.title: Task Management
GuideTasks.subtitle: Master your daily to-do list with powerful task features.
GuideTasks.basics_text: Tasks are the fundamental building blocks of Ordo Todo. Each task can be as simple as "Buy groceries" or as complex as "Design new website homepage" with subtasks, attachments, and comments.
GuideTasks.quick_add_shortcut: N (outside text fields) or Cmd/Ctrl + N
GuideTasks.quick_add_end: anywhere to create a new task
GuideTasks.or_click: Or click the "+" button in any project to add a task directly to that project.
GuideTasks.features_text: Click on any task to open the detail panel and access these powerful features:

subtasks.title: Subtasks
subtasks.description: Break complex tasks into smaller, manageable steps

due_dates.title: Due Dates
due_dates.description: Set deadlines and get timely reminders

priorities.title: Priorities
priorities.description: Mark tasks as Low, Medium, High, or Urgent

time.title: Time Estimates
time.description: Plan your day by estimating task duration

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Add files, links, and references to tasks

GuideTasks.statuses_text: Tasks move through these statuses as you work on them:
GuideTasks.priority_text: Use priorities to focus on what matters most:
GuideTasks.pro_tip_text: Use the Eisenhower Matrix view to automatically sort tasks by urgency and importance. Find it in the View menu!

GuideAnalytics.title: Analytics & Insights
GuideAnalytics.subtitle: Understand your productivity patterns with detailed data visualization.
GuideAnalytics.metrics_text: Track these essential metrics to understand and improve your productivity:

focus.title: Focus Hours
focus.description: Total time spent in focus sessions

GuideAnalytics.reports_text: Generate detailed reports to review your progress:

weekly.title: Weekly Report
weekly.description: Trends and patterns over the week

understanding.peak: Peak Hours: Find when you're most productive during the day
understanding.velocity: Task Velocity: Track how fast you complete tasks over time
understanding.ratio: Focus Ratio: Compare focus time vs total work time
understanding.goals: Goal Progress: See how close you are to weekly goals

GuideAnalytics.pro_tip_text: Review your analytics every Sunday evening. Use the insights to plan a more productive week ahead!

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: At Ordo Todo, we take your privacy seriously. This policy describes how we collect, use, and protect your personal information.

collection.title: Information Collection
collection.content: We collect information you provide directly to us, such as when you create an account, update your profile, or communicate with us.

usage.title: How we use information
usage.content: We use your information to provide, maintain, and improve our services, and to communicate with you about products, services, and events.

ai_data.title: Your data and AI
ai_data.content: AI features today run on Google Gemini: the content needed to answer (tasks, notes, context you include) is sent to Google's API under their API terms. We do not sell your data. We will publish retention and data-processing details for paid plans before billing goes live.

billing.title: Billing data
billing.content: Billing is not live yet: we do not collect payment details today. When it launches, payments will be processed by Stripe and card details will never touch our servers. Plan limits shown on the pricing page are intent until enforcement ships.

protection.title: Data Protection
protection.content: We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your personal data against unauthorized access or disclosure. Details of what exists today are listed on the security page.

sharing.title: Information Sharing
sharing.content: We do not sell your personal information. We may share data with service providers who assist in our operations, subject to strict confidentiality.

Security.title: Security
Security.subtitle: What protects your data today, what runs through third parties, and what is still planned. Anything not available today is labeled as planned.
Security.note_text: We do not claim end-to-end encryption, SOC 2 certification, or AES-256 encryption at rest: none of them are evidenced today. What follows is what verifiably exists in the product.

auth.title: Accounts and sign-in
auth.content: Sign in with email and password (passwords stored hashed with bcrypt) or with Google or GitHub OAuth. Sessions use JWT access tokens with rotating refresh tokens, revocation on logout, protection against cross-site request forgery, and rate limiting on authentication endpoints. Two-factor authentication is not available yet.

data.title: Your data
data.content: Your tasks, projects and notes live in our database and are scoped to your workspaces: you only see what you are a member of, and connected agents see no more than you do. You can export your data as JSON at any time and delete your account, which removes your data. We do not sell personal information. Encryption at rest beyond what our database provides, and certified compliance programs, are not evidenced today.

ai.title: AI and third parties
ai.content: AI features today run on Google Gemini: the content needed to answer your request is sent to Google's API under their API data terms. Nothing is sent anywhere else for AI processing. Integrations you connect (for example Google Calendar or Slack) exchange only the data needed for the feature you enabled.

billing.title: Payments
billing.content: Billing is not live yet, so we collect no payment details. When it launches, payments will be processed by Stripe and your card details will never touch our servers.

planned.title: Planned, not available
planned.content: On the roadmap: single sign-on (SSO/SAML) for organizations, a published data-processing agreement (DPA), and a path toward SOC 2. They are listed on the pricing page as planned and will be announced in the changelog when they ship.

GuideConnect.title: Connect Ordo to your assistant
GuideConnect.subtitle: Use your tasks, projects and habits from ChatGPT, Claude, Hermes or OpenClaw. No jargon: search, connect, approve.
GuideConnect.how_text: Pick whichever you prefer. Both use the same secure connection: Ordo only shows your assistant what you can see.
GuideConnect.oneclick_text: For everyone. Under 60 seconds, nothing to copy, no strange screens.
GuideConnect.manual_text: For developers and terminal tools. Ready-to-copy blocks.

chatgpt.description: Connect Ordo as an app from the directory

GuideConnectChatGPT.title: Connect Ordo to ChatGPT
GuideConnectChatGPT.subtitle: Ask ChatGPT to organize your day, create tasks or summarize your week, with your real Ordo data.
GuideConnectChatGPT.oneclick_text: You do not need to copy or understand anything technical. Just follow these steps:

1.title: Open the app directory
1.description: In ChatGPT, go to Settings, then Connected apps. Press Add app.

2.title: Search for Ordo
2.description: Type Ordo in the search box and pick the official Ordo Todo app.

3.title: Press Connect and approve
3.description: Your browser will open your Ordo account. If you were not signed in, sign in first, then press Authorize.

4.title: Go back to ChatGPT and try it
4.description: Type something like what tasks do I have today? ChatGPT will answer with your real Ordo data.

GuideConnectChatGPT.manual_text: If you use Codex or prefer to set it up by hand, add this block to your ~/.codex/config.toml file:
GuideConnectChatGPT.config_code:
[mcp_servers.ordo]
url = "https://TU-DOMINIO-ORDO/mcp"
# On first use, Codex will open the browser so you approve with your Ordo account.
GuideConnectChatGPT.verify_text: Save the file, restart Codex and ask: list my Ordo projects. If it answers with your real projects, it is connected.
GuideConnectChatGPT.verify_code: Codex › which tasks are due this week?

1.title: The browser shows an error when approving
1.fix: Close the tab, make sure you are signed in to Ordo in that browser, and try again from ChatGPT.

2.title: ChatGPT says it cannot find Ordo
2.fix: Go back to Settings, Connected apps and check that Ordo shows as connected. If not, repeat step 2.

3.title: Codex does not show Ordo tools
3.fix: Check that the URL in config.toml is exactly the one above, with no extra spaces or trailing slash, and restart Codex.

GuideConnectChatGPT.listing_text: We are publishing Ordo to the ChatGPT directory. Meanwhile, the manual setup above uses the same secure connection.

GuideConnectClaude.title: Connect Ordo to Claude
GuideConnectClaude.subtitle: Let Claude handle your planning: read your tasks, propose the day plan and execute it with you.
GuideConnectClaude.oneclick_text: You do not need to copy or understand anything technical. Just follow these steps:

1.title: Open connectors
1.description: In Claude, go to Settings, then Connectors. Press Add connector.

2.title: Search for Ordo
2.description: Type Ordo in the search box and pick the official connector.

3.title: Press Connect and approve
3.description: Your browser will open your Ordo account. If you were not signed in, sign in first, then press Authorize.

4.title: Go back to Claude and try it
4.description: Type something like organize my day. Claude will read your tasks and propose a plan.

GuideConnectClaude.manual_text: If you use the terminal, connect Ordo with a single command:
GuideConnectClaude.config_code:
claude mcp add --transport http ordo https://TU-DOMINIO-ORDO/mcp
# Then run /mcp inside Claude Code and approve in the browser.
GuideConnectClaude.verify_text: Ask: show me this quarter's objectives. If Claude answers with your real objectives, it is connected.
GuideConnectClaude.verify_code: Claude Code › /mcp  (must show ordo as connected)

1.title: The browser shows an error when approving
1.fix: Close the tab, make sure you are signed in to Ordo in that browser, and try again.

2.title: Claude Code says the server is not responding
2.fix: Run claude mcp list and check that the URL is exactly the one above. If you changed it, remove and add it again.

3.title: Claude answers without using your data
3.fix: Mention Ordo explicitly in your message, for example: using Ordo, what do I have today? That way Claude knows which connector to use.

GuideConnectClaude.listing_text: We are registering the official Ordo connector. Meanwhile, the manual command above connects to the same server.

GuideConnectHermes.title: Connect Ordo to Hermes
GuideConnectHermes.subtitle: Your memory-enabled personal helper now knows your tasks: ask it to organize you over Telegram, Discord or wherever you use it.
GuideConnectHermes.oneclick_text: You do not need to copy or understand anything technical. Just follow these steps:

1.title: Open connections
1.description: In Hermes, go to Settings, then Connections. Press Add connection.

2.title: Search for Ordo
2.description: Type Ordo in the search box and pick the official connection.

3.title: Press Connect and approve
3.description: Your browser will open your Ordo account. If you were not signed in, sign in first, then press Authorize.

4.title: Ask Hermes for something
4.description: Message your helper something like remind me of today's habits. It will answer with your real data.

GuideConnectHermes.manual_text: If you run Hermes from the terminal, add this to your ~/.hermes/config.yaml file:
GuideConnectHermes.config_code:
mcp:
  servers:
    ordo:
      url: https://TU-DOMINIO-ORDO/mcp
      auth: oauth  # Hermes will open the browser on first use
GuideConnectHermes.verify_text: Restart Hermes and ask about today's tasks. If it answers with real data, it is connected.
GuideConnectHermes.verify_code: Hermes › which habits are left today?

1.title: The browser shows an error when approving
1.fix: Close the tab, make sure you are signed in to Ordo in that browser, and try again.

2.title: Hermes says the connection failed
2.fix: Check that the URL in config.yaml is exactly the one above, with https and no trailing slash, and restart Hermes.

3.title: Hermes answers without your data
3.fix: Name Ordo in your message, for example: in Ordo, what is due tomorrow? That way Hermes knows where to look.

GuideConnectOpenClaw.title: Connect Ordo to OpenClaw
GuideConnectOpenClaw.subtitle: Run Ordo from WhatsApp, Telegram or Discord: create tasks, check your day and get summaries where you already chat.
GuideConnectOpenClaw.oneclick_text: You do not need to copy or understand anything technical. Just follow these steps:

1.title: Open the add-on marketplace
1.description: In your OpenClaw dashboard, go to Add-ons and search for Ordo in ClawHub.

2.title: Install the Ordo add-on
2.description: Press Install on the official Ordo listing and wait for it to finish.

3.title: Connect your account and approve
3.description: Press Connect. Your browser will open your Ordo account. If you were not signed in, sign in first, then press Authorize.

4.title: Talk to your assistant
4.description: Message it on your usual channel something like organize my day with Ordo. It will answer with your real plan.

GuideConnectOpenClaw.manual_text: If you manage OpenClaw from the terminal, add the remote server with this command:
GuideConnectOpenClaw.config_code:
openclaw mcp add ordo https://TU-DOMINIO-ORDO/mcp --auth oauth
# Then approve in the browser when OpenClaw asks you to.
GuideConnectOpenClaw.verify_text: Ask your assistant for the day summary. If it includes your real Ordo tasks, it is connected.
GuideConnectOpenClaw.verify_code: You › organize my day with Ordo

1.title: The browser shows an error when approving
1.fix: Close the tab, make sure you are signed in to Ordo in that browser, and try again.

2.title: OpenClaw does not list the add-on
2.fix: Refresh the ClawHub index from the dashboard and search for Ordo again. If you installed via terminal, restart the OpenClaw process.

3.title: The assistant answers without your data
3.fix: Name Ordo in your message, for example: with Ordo, what is pending? That way it uses the right connection.

GuideConnectOpenClaw.listing_text: The @ordo-todo/openclaw-plugin package is ready and under review for ClawHub. Meanwhile you can install it from the repository.

GuideConnectSlack.title: Use Ordo inside Slack
GuideConnectSlack.subtitle: Attach Ordo to Slackbot to check and create tasks without leaving your channels.

1.title: Open your Slack app settings
1.description: Go to your Slack workspace settings and open Apps.

2.title: Add Ordo as a server
2.description: In the external servers section, add the Ordo address and choose to sign in with your account when asked.

3.title: Approve in the browser
3.description: Your Ordo account will open. If you were not signed in, sign in first, then press Authorize.

4.title: Enable Ordo in Slackbot
4.description: Open a direct message with Slackbot, go to Apps and enable Ordo with the + button.

5.title: Pick your permissions
5.description: The first time Ordo wants to act, Slack will ask you: allow once, always allow or deny. You decide.

GuideConnectSlack.permissions_text: Ordo can only see what you see. Every action (creating a task, for example) asks your permission the first time, and you can change it anytime from Slackbot.

GuideConnectZapier.title: Connect Ordo with Zapier
GuideConnectZapier.subtitle: Use Ordo alongside thousands of apps through Zapier, while native integrations are on the way.

1.title: Create a new Zap
1.description: In Zapier, press Create Zap and pick the app that triggers the automation (for example, Gmail).

2.title: Add the Ordo step
2.description: As the action, search for Ordo and pick what you want to do, like creating a task.

3.title: Connect your account and approve
3.description: Zapier will ask you to connect your Ordo account. Your browser will open: sign in if needed and press Authorize.

4.title: Test and turn on
4.description: Send a test from Zapier, check that the task shows up in Ordo, and turn the Zap on.

GuideConnectZapier.example_text: When an email marked important arrives, create an Ordo task with the subject as the title:
GuideConnectZapier.example_code:
Trigger: Gmail › New important email
Action: Ordo › Create task
  Title: {{email subject}}
  Project: Inbox
GuideConnectZapier.listing_text: We are preparing the official Ordo app on Zapier. Meanwhile, the documented bridge above covers both directions.

GuideMore.title: Features you may not know
GuideMore.subtitle: All of this already exists in Ordo today. Each block describes where to find it in the app.

meetings.title: AI meetings
meetings.description: Paste your meeting transcript and extract actions, summaries and tasks automatically. Input is manual: Ordo does not record your calls.

workload.title: Team workload
workload.description: See who carries what in your workspace: per-member load, balancing suggestions and personal view.

wellbeing.title: Wellbeing and burnout
wellbeing.description: Gentle alerts when your load spikes, weekly wellbeing summary and a dedicated page.

search.title: Smart search
search.description: Find tasks, projects and habits instantly, with suggestions and direct questions.

coach.title: Chat coach
coach.description: AI conversations about your productivity, with insights based on your data.

gamification.title: Gamification
gamification.description: XP, levels and achievements for completing tasks and streaks. Your progress, celebrated.

focusAudio.title: Focus audio
focusAudio.description: Ambient sound generated in-app for your focus sessions. No external subscriptions.

GuideWorkspaces.title: Workspaces
GuideWorkspaces.subtitle: One container per area of your life: projects, people and activity, cleanly separated.
GuideWorkspaces.what_text: It is the highest level of organization. Projects, tasks, notes and tags live inside a workspace, so personal never mixes with work or with each client.
GuideWorkspaces.what_switch_text: The sidebar selector decides which workspace you are viewing: switch it and the tasks, calendar and notes you see change too. Everything stays where it belongs.
GuideWorkspaces.roles_text: Every member joins with a role. The hierarchy is simple and strict:
GuideWorkspaces.invite_text: From the workspace settings (Members tab) you invite by email and choose each person's role.
GuideWorkspaces.invite_box_text: You can cancel pending invitations, change roles later, and any member can leave the workspace on their own (except the owner).
GuideWorkspaces.activity_text: The workspace side panel shows a log of the latest actions: who created what, who joined, what moved.
GuideWorkspaces.activity_box_text: It is an audit log of the workspace's latest actions. "View all activity" opens the full record.
GuideWorkspaces.pro_tip_text: Start with three workspaces: Personal, Work and one for your current big client or project. Switching context is one click.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Created the workspace: invites, manages members and is the only one who can delete it.

admin.title: Admin
admin.description: Manages members, settings and activity. Can also invite.

member.title: Member
member.description: Works normally and creates projects inside the workspace.

viewer.title: Viewer
viewer.description: Read-only: sees content without changing anything.

GuideGoals.title: Goals (OKRs)
GuideGoals.subtitle: Big goals measured with numbers: the OKR method, inside Ordo.
GuideGoals.okr_text: An Objective is the qualitative goal ("grow as a consultant"). Its Key Results are the metrics that prove progress ("3 new clients"). Together they form an OKR with its own progress bar.
GuideGoals.create_box_text: "New Objective" asks for title, description, period (quarterly, yearly or custom), color and dates. Average progress shows up on the dashboard right away.
GuideGoals.kr_title: Key Results: pick the metric type
GuideGoals.kr_text: Each KR supports five metric types, and Ordo fills in sensible values when you pick one:
GuideGoals.link_text: KRs can be linked to concrete tasks: every completed task pushes the KR, and the KR pushes the objective's bar — no manual counting.
GuideGoals.link_box_text: When creating or editing a task you can attach it to a Key Result. The KR shows how many tasks are linked.
GuideGoals.review_text: The screen tabs separate Active, Completed and At Risk. At-risk objectives are the ones that need a decision, not just effort.
GuideGoals.pro_tip_text: Two or three measurable KRs per objective. If it does not fit in a number, it is not a Key Result yet: sharpen it until it does.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Revenue and savings, with a monetary unit.

boolean.title: Yes / No
boolean.description: Binary milestones: published or not, signed or not.

tasks.title: Completed tasks
tasks.description: Automatically counts tasks linked to the KR.

GuideNotes.title: Sticky Notes
GuideNotes.subtitle: Fast capture without friction: one post-it per idea, no statuses or dates.
GuideNotes.what_text: Notes are each workspace's capture zone: ideas, quick reminders and thoughts that do not deserve a task yet. You write; they save themselves.
GuideNotes.modes_text: Choose how to see your post-its depending on the moment:
GuideNotes.perks_text: They are simple on purpose, but nothing is missing:
GuideNotes.from_idea_text: When a note matures, turn it into a task with a project and date, then delete the note. Notes capture; tasks commit.
GuideNotes.pro_tip_text: Give each color a fixed meaning (yellow = idea, pink = urgent, green = learning) and the color filter becomes your classification system.

wall.title: Wall
wall.description: Tidy grid: search, filter by color and edit cleanly.

board.title: Board
board.description: Free canvas: drag each note and group it wherever; position is saved.

colors.title: Six colors
colors.description: Change a note's color on the fly with its palette.

search.title: Filter and search
search.description: Find the note among hundreds by color or text.

GuideEisenhower.title: Eisenhower Matrix
GuideEisenhower.subtitle: Two questions — urgent? important? — to decide what comes now.
GuideEisenhower.what_text: The matrix sorts your pending tasks into four quadrants by urgency and importance. Ordo proposes a classification; the final call is yours.
GuideEisenhower.quadrants_text: Each quadrant comes with a clear next action:
GuideEisenhower.drag_text: Move tasks between quadrants by dragging: on drop, their real priority changes in the app (Do First = urgent, Schedule = high, Delegate = medium, Delete = low).
GuideEisenhower.when_text: It is the perfect triage exercise for Monday morning… or for any moment when everything seems urgent at once. Completing tasks is one click, without leaving the matrix.
GuideEisenhower.pro_tip_text: Dragging to "Delete" does not remove the task: it only lowers its priority so it stops getting in the way. Real deleting still happens in Tasks.

do.title: Do First
do.description: Urgent and important: today, hands on.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: Important, not urgent: it deserves a calendar slot.

delegate.title: Delegate
delegate.description: Urgent, not important: a candidate for new hands.

delete.title: Delete
delete.description: Neither urgent nor important: lower its priority so it stops getting in the way.

GuideMeetings.title: Meeting Assistant
GuideMeetings.subtitle: Paste the transcript and turn the talk into a summary, decisions and tasks.
GuideMeetings.how_text: Copy the transcript from your video call (or jot the dialogue down by hand) and paste it into the Meetings screen area. One click and the AI does the rest.
GuideMeetings.paste_box_text: The format is simple: "Name: what they said", one line per speaker. If the first line is the meeting title, your history will stay tidy.
GuideMeetings.analyze_box_text: "Analyze with AI" extracts the conversation's structure and saves the meeting to your history automatically.
GuideMeetings.output_text: Four blocks per meeting, all reviewable and collapsible:
GuideMeetings.convert_text: Every action item carries an owner, a due date and a priority badge. The "Convert to Tasks" button creates them all at once as real Ordo tasks, ready for the calendar and the matrix.
GuideMeetings.history_box_text: The latest analyzed meetings are kept: one click reloads their transcript and analysis when someone asks "what did we agree on?".
GuideMeetings.pro_tip_text: Input is manual and private: Ordo never records your calls. Paste only what you want analyzed.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The meeting's point in a paragraph, with key points and topics.

actions.title: Action Items
actions.description: What was agreed, who owns it and by when, with priority.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.description: What was decided, by whom, with the exact context.

people.title: Participants
people.description: Who was there and what role they played.

GuideCoach.title: Coach Chat
GuideCoach.subtitle: Talk with the assistant to plan, prioritize and decide with judgment.
GuideCoach.what_text: The chat connects to an assistant that advises on your productivity: how to split the day, what to tackle first, how to structure breaks. It helps you think; then you execute in Tasks or the plan.
GuideCoach.starters_text: Four ready-made suggestions save you the blank page:
GuideCoach.ask_text: Answer quality depends on the context you give. Mention deadlines, available time and what is truly urgent.
GuideCoach.ask_box_text: "I have 12 tasks and 3 hours, where do I start?" gets better advice than "help with my tasks". Iterate: reply with more detail and refine.
GuideCoach.limits_title: Know what it is (and is not)
GuideCoach.limits_text: The coach is advisory: it gives advice but does not create or move tasks from the chat. And like any AI, it can be wrong.
GuideCoach.limits_box_text: Treat its answers as a starting point, not a verdict. Conversations are saved per session: copy what matters before closing.
GuideCoach.pro_tip_text: Enter sends the message; Shift + Enter adds a line break.
